name: LMB (Laxmi Misthan Bhandar)
top_review: An institution in Jaipur since 1954. The raj kachori alone is worth the trip. Dal baati churma is authentic and delicious. Always crowded — go early or late to avoid queue. Pure vegetarian, very hygienic.
text: LMB (Laxmi Misthan Bhandar) is Jaipur's most iconic vegetarian restaurant and sweet shop since 1954. Rating 4.4/5 from 8200+ reviews. Located in Johari Bazaar, Old City. Budget-friendly — full meal under ₹300. Famous for raj kachori (crispy shell with yogurt, chutneys), dal baati churma, pyaaz kachori, and a legendary sweets counter with ghewar, malpua, sohan halwa. Pure vegetarian, Jain options available. A must-visit for authentic Rajasthani food. Opens 8am for breakfast kachori.

name: Suvarna Mahal
dietary: vegetarian and non-vegetarian, Jain on advance notice
address: Jai Mahal Palace, Jacob Road, Civil Lines, Jaipur
top_review: Dining under Venetian chandeliers in a 250-year-old ballroom is surreal. The royal Rajasthani thali has 18 courses. Laal maas (red mutton curry) is some of the best I've ever had. Worth every rupee for a special occasion.
text: Suvarna Mahal at Jai Mahal Palace is Jaipur's premier fine-dining restaurant inside a stunning ballroom with gold-gilded ceilings. Rating 4.5/5 from 1800 reviews. ₹3500+ per person. Famous for royal Rajasthani thali with 18 dishes, authentic laal maas (spicy red mutton curry), safed maas (white mutton curry), ker sangri (desert beans). Dress code applies. Reservation required. Exceptional for special occasions and anniversary dinners.

name: Tapri Central
address: E-8 Subhash Marg, near Clock Tower, Civil Lines, Jaipur
top_review: Jaipur's coolest chai spot. Hipster vibe with authentic flavours. The masala chai is some of the best in India. Morning kachori breakfast is a ritual. Perfect place to sit, sip and people-watch. Very affordable.
text: Tapri Central is Jaipur's most beloved chai and breakfast cafe. Rating 4.5/5 from 11000+ reviews. Budget — under ₹200/person. Famous for exceptional masala chai, cutting chai, morning kachori breakfast, tapri thali. Retro decor, open terrace, very popular with locals and travellers. Open from 8am — ideal breakfast stop before sightseeing. Cash-only. Near Civil Lines, easy auto access from Jaipur station.

name: Chokhi Dhani Village Resort
top_review: Best cultural evening experience in Rajasthan. Not just a restaurant — it's a full village. Folk dances, puppet shows, henna, camel rides, then sit on charpoys and eat a massive authentic thali. Entry fee includes dinner. Great for families.
text: Chokhi Dhani is a heritage Rajasthani village resort 9 km from Jaipur on Tonk Road. Rating 4.2/5 from 14000 reviews. Entry + dinner ₹900/person. A full cultural experience — folk dances, puppet shows, magic, camel rides, henna, music — then authentic Rajasthani thali dinner served on banana leaf while sitting on charpoys. Best cultural evening in Jaipur. Go for sunset (5pm onwards). Purely vegetarian. 12 km from old city — book cab.

name: Ambrai Restaurant
address: Amet Haveli, Chandpol, Lake Pichola, Udaipur 313001
top_review: The most beautiful restaurant view I've ever experienced. Sitting lakeside with City Palace and Lake Palace in front of you at sunset is extraordinary. Food is good — the dal baati churma and the fish tikka are excellent. Go for sunset.
text: Ambrai is Udaipur's most scenically positioned restaurant, sitting directly on Lake Pichola with front-row views of City Palace, Lake Palace, and Jagmandir. Rating 4.5/5 from 7600+ reviews. Moderate pricing ₹800/person. Famous for sunset dining — tables on the lakeside terrace. Dal baati churma, Rajasthani thali, fresh fish. Bar available (rare in Udaipur's old city). Book a terrace table in advance for sunset hours. Cash and cards accepted.

name: Natraj Dining Hall
top_review: Best value thali in Udaipur. ₹180 for unlimited Rajasthani thali with refills — dal, sabzi, roti, rice, papad, achaar. Locals eat here. Food is home-style and authentic. No ambience but the food is real.
text: Natraj Dining Hall is Udaipur's most beloved budget thali restaurant. Rating 4.3/5 from 3400 reviews. Unlimited Rajasthani thali for ₹150-200. Home-style cooking, generous portions, fast service. Very popular with locals, students and budget travellers. Pure vegetarian. Near Bapu Bazaar market area. Open for lunch and dinner. Best at lunchtime when food is freshest.

name: Mishrilal Hotel
top_review: BEST LASSI IN INDIA. The makhaniya lassi is thick, cold, saffron-flavored perfection in a kulhad. I had three glasses. The mawa kachori is also outstanding — sweet, flaky, indulgent. A must for every Jodhpur visitor. Very cheap.
text: Mishrilal Hotel is Jodhpur's most famous snack shop, legendary for its makhaniya lassi. Rating 4.6/5 from 5200+ reviews. Budget — lassi ₹80, kachori ₹25-60. Located in Sardar Market near Clock Tower. The makhaniya lassi is Jodhpur's signature drink — thick saffron-cream lassi served in a kulhad (clay cup). Also famous for mawa kachori (sweet kachori with mawa filling). Opens 8am. Go before 10am to avoid queues. Cash only. Featured in multiple food travel shows.

name: Indique Restaurant
address: Heritage Inn, High Court Road, Jodhpur 342001
top_review: Spectacular rooftop fort views. The laal maas is absolutely authentic and fiery. Cocktail menu is excellent — try the Blue City Negroni. Service is attentive and the sunset window is incredible. Worth the price.
text: Indique is Jodhpur's finest rooftop restaurant with direct Mehrangarh Fort views. Rating 4.4/5 from 3800 reviews. Moderate pricing ₹900/person. Famous for laal maas (Rajasthani spicy mutton), masala chaas, rooftop cocktail bar. The fort lights up at dusk and dining becomes magical. Reservation strongly recommended for sunset. Heritage Inn property. Award-winning kitchen.

name: Trio Restaurant
address: Gandhi Darshan, Near Amar Sagar Pol, Jaisalmer 345001
top_review: Best rooftop in Jaisalmer for fort views. The ker sangri (local desert beans) is incredible and unlike anything I've had elsewhere. Camel milk kulfi is a unique dessert experience. Friendly staff, fair prices.
text: Trio Restaurant is Jaisalmer's most celebrated mid-range rooftop restaurant near the fort. Rating 4.3/5 from 4100 reviews. Moderate pricing ₹600/person. Famous for fort-view dining, ker sangri (Jaisalmer's signature vegetable dish), camel milk kulfi, and Rajasthani thali. Rooftop catches the golden fort light perfectly at sunset. Cooking classes available. Very popular with international travellers.

name: The Hammir Dining Hall
top_review: Practical and good value for Ranthambore. The early morning breakfast before safari is exactly what you need — chai, parathas, eggs. The jungle thali at dinner is hearty. Nothing fancy but solid food in an area with limited options.
text: Hammir Dining Hall is the most practical dining option for safari travellers in Ranthambore. Rating 3.9/5 from 480 reviews. Budget ₹350/person. Early breakfast from 6am for pre-safari meals — chai, parathas, eggs, poha. Lunch and dinner thalis (vegetarian and non-veg). Limited dining options exist in the Ranthambore area so most properties include or recommend meals on-site. Safari timings affect meal windows — confirm with your stay.

name: Raju's Restaurant
top_review: Pushkar has a huge Israeli traveller community so restaurants here are special. Raju's has amazing falafel and hummus, incredible lassi, and a perfect rooftop lake view. Very budget-friendly. The shakshouka is surprisingly authentic.
text: Raju's Restaurant is Pushkar's famous backpacker cafe known for excellent Israeli-Indian fusion food. Rating 4.3/5 from 2100 reviews. Budget ₹250/person. Note: Pushkar is a holy town — ALL restaurants are 100% vegetarian and no alcohol/eggs served. Raju's famous for falafel, hummus, shakshuka, Israeli breakfast, and classic Indian thali. Rooftop with lake view. Great for breakfast. Popular with international backpackers.
